decisions.reason: It is very close to the firm's core dosimetry and calibration knowledge and its continued home-page prominence suggests strong fit and enough early traction to justify ongoing support.

The software builds on the firm's existing oncology QA workflows and integration capabilities, so its absorptive capacity is high and the firm is well placed to refine it through in-house R&D and clinical feedback.
A CT image quality phantom extends the firm's established medical imaging QA base, and as an expanding R&D-active firm it is likely to keep the product long enough to learn and improve it.

This mammography phantom is more distant from the firm's strongest knowledge base, so the expected learning and improvement benefits are weaker and management is more likely to reallocate resources to closer QA lines.

As another mammography-specific phantom outside the firm's core radiation therapy and broader imaging QA strengths, it faces the highest risk of pruning if early demand and learning signals are not clearly superior.
Medical imaging QA instruments fit the firm's stated direction of measurement, integration, and automation, and the firm's existing capabilities make commercial improvement and support credible.
